key_insight: Spray angle is the dominant handling parameter in cold-sprayed Inconel 718, strongly affecting deposition, porosity, tensile strength, and surface roughness, while microhardness stays essentially unchanged.
engineering_relevance: For repair and coating of turbine components, optimizing gun orientation can improve coating quality and process efficiency without necessarily changing hardness.
method: High-pressure cold spray of Inconel 718 using nitrogen as the process gas
Varied spray angle, standoff distance, and traverse speed of the spray gun
Evaluated microhardness, porosity, roughness, tensile strength, microstructure, and sliding wear
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the lowest spray angle (90°) produced the most defects and the lowest deposition rate, and that wear behavior was not significantly affected by spray angle.
watch_item: The results are parameter- and setup-specific, so the optimal spray settings may not transfer directly to other powders, substrates, or gas-spray systems.
paper_title: Influence of the Spray Angle, Standoff Distance, and Traverse Speed of the Spray Gun on the Tribomechanical Properties of Cold-Sprayed Inconel 718 Coatings
